title: Rate limit & throttling runbook — observability notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc captures observability primitives, metric definitions, tracing conventions, dashboard sketches and first-pass alert thresholds for investigating rate-limit and throttling incidents across Redwood’s inference surface (hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments). Focus is operational detection + rapid mitigation, not deeper long-term capacity planning (that belongs in capacity-playbook).

Why this is separate:
- Rate-limit incidents are noisy and easily misattributed to model regressions or infra flakiness.
- Throttling often spans multiple layers (API gateway, routing policy, model variant fallback, dedicated pool manager). We need a minimal but actionable instrumentation story to isolate the layer deciding to throttle.

Unresolved questions / open decisions (TODO):
- Should the per-tenant token_bucket_fill_rate be recorded at 1s or 10s resolution? (tradeoff: higher resolution helps fast triage but increases cardinality)
- How much PII-safe context do we attach to trace spans for tenant IDs in shared-hosted? Use hashed tenant ids by default.
- Default severity mapping for throttling alerts (S1/S2) needs alignment with oncall rota.

Metric definitions (prometheus-friendly names + intent):
- throttle.events_total: counter, labels {scope, tenant_hash, region, model_family, decision_point, reason} — increments whenever a throttle decision is returned to caller (HTTP 429 or queued+drop).
- throttle.rate_ratio: gauge, computed as throttle.events_total / incoming.requests_total over window. Provides a quick proportion of requests throttled.
- throttle.latency_added_ms: histogram summary of additional latency introduced by queueing/backpressure before final decision (buckets: 0,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000).
- token_bucket.fill_rate_per_sec: gauge, labels {tenant_hash, pool} — tokens added/sec to tenant bucket; useful to detect misconfiguration or sudden drop in refill (kube node pressure).
- token_bucket.available_tokens: gauge, labels {tenant_hash, pool} — current token count; essential for root cause (policy vs surge).
- queue.drops_total: counter, labels {pool, model_variant, region, reason} — counts backend drops when queue size exceeds cap before throttle decision is surfaced upstream.
- routed_fallbacks_total: counter, labels {original_model, fallback_model, tenant_hash} — tracks automatic model variant fallback events triggered by capacity constraints.
- client_retry_header_rate: gauge, labels {tenant_hash} — percent of requests with retry headers present (client behaviour can amplify throttle storms).
- throttle.sla_breach_ratio: gauge — fraction of requests hitting configured tenant SLA for latency because of throttling.

Tracing / span conventions (OpenTelemetry recommendations):
- Each request path must include a top-level span "req.gateway" with attributes: tenant.hash, route.id, api_key_anon, region.
- When a rate-limit check is executed, create child span: "policy.rate_limit_check" with attributes: policy.id, decision_point (gateway|router|pool), tokens_required, tokens_remaining, refill_rate, window_ms. Log event "rate_limit_result" with outcome {allow, delay, throttle}.
- If queuing occurs, attach a span "req.queue_wait" with duration = time spent in local queue. Attach metric sample throttle.latency_added_ms.
- When a fallback / routing change is triggered due to capacity, emit span "routing.fallback" with attributes original_model, chosen_model, reason_code. This span should include stack trace snapshot (first 3 frames) for debugging config code paths.
- Sample traces: low-latency path, queued-then-allowed, queued-then-throttled, immediate-throttle. Instrumentation examples (pseudo-otel):
  tracer.startSpan('policy.rate_limit_check', {attributes: { 'policy.id': 'tenant_burst_1', 'decision_point':'gateway', 'tokens_required': 120, 'tokens_remaining': 0 }})
  recordEvent('rate_limit_result', {outcome:'throttle', reason:'burst_limit_exceeded'})

Dashboard suggestions (Grafana panel ideas + queries):
- "Throttle heatmap by tenant" — stacked bar heatmap showing throttle.events_total per tenant_hash over 5m. Drilldown link to tenant page.
- "Throttle ratio + incoming RPS" — dual-axis panel: incoming.requests RPS and throttle.rate_ratio. Useful to see if ratio rises with traffic.
- "Token bucket evictions" — table of tenant_hash, avg_available_tokens last 1h, refill_rate, last_throttle_time; color-coded thresholds.
- "Queue pressure lanes" — histogram of queue.drops_total and queue.size_by_pool.
- "Fallbacks by original model" — count of routed_fallbacks_total, with churn rate (fallbacks/min).
- "Trace samples" — quick links to representative spans for patterns (immediate_429, queued_allow, queued_drop).

PromQL examples (first-pass):
- throttle_rate_ratio (1m): sum(rate(throttle.events_total[1m])) / sum(rate(incoming.requests_total[1m]))
- tenants_exceeding_threshold (5m): topk(20, sum by (tenant_hash) (rate(throttle.events_total[5m])) )
- avg_token_avail (10m): avg_over_time(token_bucket.available_tokens[10m])

Alerting (first-pass thresholds — tuned after incident data):
- P0: system-wide throttle rate > 15% sustained for 2m AND customer-facing 429 spike across >= 3 regions -> page oncall SRE and product oncall.
- P1: single tenant throttle_rate > 40% sustained for 5m -> page account-eng and SRE; include tenant hash in alert.
- P2: token_bucket.fill_rate_per_sec for control-plane < 10% of configured refill on more than 2 nodes -> slack alert to infra.
- Rule: include small sample of correlated traces in the alert payload (trace ids for up to 5 traces).

Runbook steps (triage play):
1) Confirm alerts and gather context: affected tenants (tenant_hash), regions, route ids, models.
2) Open quick dashboard panels (Throttle ratio + RPS, Token bucket table, Queue pressure lanes). Grab top 3 sample traces.
3) Identify decision_point from span attributes: gateway vs router vs pool. If gateway: check API gateway config and recent deploys (linked PRs). If router/pool: inspect pool autoscale and node-level metrics.
4) Mitigate timeline:
   - If burst surge from small set of tenants: temporarily increase per-tenant burst allowance or apply per-tenant soft-fail policy (allow with rate-limited response header).
   - If controller/pool underprovisioned: activate burst capacity (dedicated autoscale policy) or reroute traffic to secondary pool.
   - If global throttling due to misconfiguration: rollback recent rate-limit config change (concourse/PR rollback).
5) Communicate: post incident status to #prod-incidents with short summary, affected tenants, mitigation step and ETA.
6) Post-incident: run a short postmortem, populate the metrics and trace anchors, propose instrumentation gaps.

Example quick checklist for oncall (copyable):
- [ ] Open "Throttle ratio + RPS" panel and confirm ratio > 0.
- [ ] Grab top 3 traces from last 5 minutes with decision_point attribute.
- [ ] Check token_bucket.available_tokens for top affected tenants.
- [ ] If queue.drops_total > 0: consider temporarily raising queue cap for specific pool.
- [ ] Apply mitigation and monitor throttle.rate_ratio for decay.

Privacy & cardinality guardrails:
- Tenant identifiers stored in metrics must be hashed (sha256 with short prefix) to avoid exposing PII in dashboards. Use tenant_hash label with 8 char prefix.
- Cap cardinality: only surface tenant_hash on drilldown panels; default overview panels aggregate by region/model.
- Sample traces for alerts only include anonymized tenant_hash; full tenant id requires walled access.

Notes to self / quick hacks observed in past incidents:
- Some clients retry aggressively when they get 429s and set no jitter, creating a retry storm. We should surface client_retry_header_rate to detect this pattern early.
- TTL on token_bucket.available_tokens metrics was set to 1s in a past deploy and created an explosion of timeseries under high throughput; bump aggregation to 10s by default.
- In early experiments, routing.fallback spans were missing attributes about the routing table version; add route.version attribute to help correlate to config changes.

Follow-ups and next steps (owners):
- Add trace attribute route.version to routing.fallback spans (owner: Miguel Ortega) — JIRA-8472
- Prototype a tenant-level burst simulator to replay throttle patterns for dashboards (owner: Ravi Shah) — CON-220 followup
- Run data-backfill to compute realistic alert thresholds from 90-day data (owner: Clara Jensen)

Links & references:
- Confluence playbook (draft): https://redwood-confluence/internal/OBS-220
- Related perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421
- Incident example (postmortem): JIRA-3124

This doc is intentionally practical and minimal — aim for fast triage. Keep instrumentation lightweight (small set of counters + a handful of decision-point spans) and avoid exploding cardinality. Happy to iterate after first few incidents.

----
Choppy notes / scratch area (feel free to edit):
- sample promql to surface per-region throttle spikes: sum by(region) (rate(throttle.events_total[1m])) / sum by(region) (rate(incoming.requests_total[1m]))
- possible new metric: "throttle.latency_percentile_95_added" as gauge computed by pipeline for faster alerting.
- think about a small synthetic that ramps a single tenant to validate token_bucket semantics in dedicated pools.
